title: Acorn emulation, Gold Box archaeology and legacy-disk discovery
summary: Review eight canonical candidates, promote seven projects, and advance the Acorn/BBC relationship graph
notes: The CPU audit queue returned zero unresolved source/target CPU areas, so no CPU value was inferred merely to satisfy a quota. The older Acorn/BBC profile task was selected from the canonical queue. Reviewed candidate URLs: mattgodbolt/jsbeeb, kieranhj/beebjit-libretro, tom-seddon/beeblink, malcyon/wish, kieranhj/stnicc-beeb, medamap/Legacy89DiskKit and ernop/nectaris-remake were promoted; N0zoM1z0/th04 resolved to the existing promoted TH04 record and was not duplicated. Fresh GitHub code/README searches were exactly 'PC-98 disassembly reconstruction', 'Atari Lynx toolchain homebrew', and 'Oric disassembly reassembly toolchain'. The PC-98 route surfaced the already indexed TH04 and Legacy89DiskKit; the latter qualified on its documented Japanese disk/filesystem support. The Lynx and Oric routes produced only broad indexes, emulator distributions, unrelated modern code or already indexed references, with no additional candidate selected for deep review. STNICCC is recorded as a BBC fan recreation, Nectaris as a from-scratch researched remake, and neither is relabelled as binary-derived reverse engineering. Read-only review: no emulator, ROM, disk image, compiler, game, server or hardware was run.

project.title: jsbeeb — JavaScript BBC Micro-family emulator

runtime_profiles.name: Browser build
runtime_profiles.os: Chrome 111+, Edge 111+, Firefox 115+, Safari 16.4+ or iOS Safari 16.4+
runtime_profiles.notes: The package browserslist states these browser floors; no host CPU or RAM minimum is stated.

runtime_profiles.name: Source and desktop build
runtime_profiles.notes: The package manifest states the Node floor and documents optional Electron packaging; no host CPU or RAM minimum is stated.

project.status: Active browser and Electron emulator with debugger, rewind, media inspection and automated CPU tests; not independently built or run in this review.

evidence: Latest reviewed upstream commit explicitly says it was generated with Claude Code and credits Claude Opus 5.5: https://github.com/mattgodbolt/jsbeeb/commit/178031ec9e7420a0965981f7f7877df35886fe0c

identity.narrative: jsbeeb is the canonical JavaScript BBC Micro-family emulator maintained by Matt Godbolt.

classification.narrative: It qualifies as a core emulator, debugger and media-analysis environment directly useful to BBC development and archaeology.

source_cpu.narrative: The model implementation explicitly selects MOS 6502, CMOS 65C02 and CMOS 65C12 opcode families.

target_cpu.narrative: Browser and Electron builds do not establish one fixed native output CPU; no host architecture is inferred.

build.narrative: The README and package manifest document npm development, test, web build and Electron packaging paths.
build.limitations: The tracker did not install dependencies, compile, package or run the emulator.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The package manifest gives exact supported browser floors and Node.js 24.15.0+ for source/desktop builds; no CPU or RAM minimum is stated.

ai.narrative: The reviewed head commit explicitly attributes generation to Claude Code and co-authorship to Claude Opus 5.5.

relationships.narrative: The separately tracked jsbeeb-mcp project exposes this emulator through MCP; that automation layer does not replace the emulator record.

project.title: beebjit-libretro — BBC Micro JIT emulator core for RetroArch
project.display_title: beebjit-libretro — BBC Micro JIT emulator core for RetroArch

runtime_profiles.name: RG40XXV muOS tested target
runtime_profiles.min_cpu: Allwinner H700 quad Cortex-A53 is the documented first tested target, not a claimed minimum
runtime_profiles.notes: The README reports full-speed BBC emulation on this device and says the JIT requires a 64-bit host. No RAM minimum is stated.

project.status: Linux-only libretro wrapper around beebjit with ARM64/x64 JIT support and documented RG40XXV measurements; not independently built or benchmarked.

evidence: README states the core was written with Claude Code under Kieran Connell's direction.

identity.narrative: This repository is the distinct libretro glue layer around Chris Evans' beebjit emulator.

classification.narrative: It qualifies as a BBC emulator integration and debugging/benchmark environment rather than a new independent CPU core.

source_cpu.narrative: The README explicitly describes beebjit's JIT as 6502-only and the interpreter option as the 6502 core.

target_cpu.narrative: The README explicitly limits the JIT to ARM64 and x64 64-bit Linux hosts and documents an aarch64 cross-build.

build.narrative: Native Linux make and Zig-based aarch64 cross-build commands are documented along with headless test and benchmark scripts.
build.limitations: The tracker did not compile the core, connect to a handheld, run RetroArch or reproduce performance figures.

runtime_profiles.narrative: An RG40XXV with Allwinner H700 quad Cortex-A53 running muOS is an explicitly measured target; this is retained as a tested profile, not generalized into a minimum.

ai.narrative: The README explicitly says Claude Code wrote the core from Kieran Connell's direction; the reviewed head commit also credits Claude Opus 5.5.

relationships.narrative: The core wraps beebjit as a submodule and says its repository adds only libretro glue and two OS substitutions.

project.title: beeb-niccc — BBC Micro STNICCC-2000 recreation

runtime_profiles.name: BBC disc build
runtime_profiles.notes: The Makefile builds DSD images and names B/Acorn 1770 and Master 128 emulator configurations; no minimum CPU, RAM or model is claimed.

project.status: Released BBC Micro recreation of the STNICCC-2000 demo with BeebAsm source, stream encoders and BBC/NuLA/CPC-palette variants; not independently assembled or run.

evidence: The reviewed v1.2 commit explicitly credits Claude Opus 5.5 and links its Claude Code session: https://github.com/kieranhj/stnicc-beeb/commit/9a9cce3a80e71648fe7396552c4531a8b64a4a08

identity.narrative: The repository is the BBC Micro recreation of STNICCC-2000 released as beeb-niccc.

classification.narrative: This is a substantial native fan recreation/conversion and demo production, not a disassembly or binary-derived source reconstruction.

source_cpu.narrative: The BBC work consumes an STNICCC scene stream rather than reconstructing the original demo executable, so an original-binary source CPU is not assigned.

target_cpu.narrative: The build labels the source as BeebAsm/.6502 assembly and assembles the BBC disc output from that code.

build.narrative: The Makefile documents BeebAsm, Exomizer and Python stages that build SSD/DSD release media and test routes through b2/jsbeeb.
build.limitations: The tracker did not assemble the demo, generate media or run an emulator.

runtime_profiles.narrative: BBC and Master emulator configurations are named, but the reviewed primary files do not state a minimum model, RAM amount or chipset requirement.

ai.narrative: The reviewed v1.2 commit explicitly credits Claude Opus 5.5 and a Claude Code session.

relationships.narrative: The repository adapts the STNICCC-2000 scene for BBC hardware and includes its own encoders/build; it is not a fork or mirror of the original Atari ST binary.

identity.narrative: Legacy89DiskKit is the canonical CLI/library for Japanese 8-bit and 16-bit disk container and filesystem workflows.

classification.narrative: It qualifies as disk/filesystem analysis and development tooling, not as an emulator or reconstructed native application.

source_cpu.narrative: The reviewed inputs are disk containers, filesystems and boot metadata rather than one original machine-code binary.

target_cpu.narrative: The toolkit manipulates disk data and does not emit a native retro executable with a target CPU.

build.narrative: Shell and PowerShell build scripts run managed builds/tests and conditionally build/test the C++ library through CMake.
build.limitations: The tracker did not build either implementation or open a disk image.

runtime_profiles.narrative: Windows, Linux and macOS install/build routes are documented; no host CPU, RAM or OS-version minimum is stated.

ai.narrative: No explicit development-AI attribution was found in the reviewed README or platform support document; agent-oriented planning filenames alone are not treated as contribution evidence.

relationships.narrative: The C# CLI/library and documented C++ native bridge are one product family in the same repository, not separate titled projects.
